title: DR1's country list carries the 27 EU member states plus 11 EU overseas territories and 3 Crown Dependencies; the frontend offers 27 member states plus four EFTA countries and no territories at all, on both the origin and the destination question.

finding.frontend: Country of origin and Destination country both offer the same 31 entries: the 27 EU member states plus Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland. No territory or Crown Dependency appears. Both pages read one function — src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/origin/controller.js:57-61 and src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/destination-country/controller.js:24-28 both call countries.originCountries() — and that is filled from the reference-data service's /countries endpoint for the GBNAG_SPS_EX block at src/server/app/services/countries/index.js:11. Three member states are also named differently from DR1: Czechia, Ireland and Netherlands (the).
finding.prototype: The list is 41 entries, alphabetical, and the same list serves the origin question and both destination-country reveals. It is the 27 member states, then 11 EU overseas territories written as "territory (parent)" — Azores (Portugal), Canary Islands (Spain), Ceuta (Spain), French Guiana (France), Guadeloupe (France), Madeira (Portugal), Martinique (France), Mayotte (France), Melilla (Spain), Reunion (France), Saint Martin (France) — and 3 Crown Dependencies, Guernsey (United Kingdom), Isle of Man (United Kingdom) and Jersey (United Kingdom). It carries no EFTA country: Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland are absent. DR1 names the member states Czech Republic, Republic of Ireland and Netherlands.
finding.difference: The list a user picks from has to become DR1's 41 entries, on both pages, including the parent country in each territory label. The frontend does not own the list — the names come from reference data's GBNAG_SPS_EX block — so the territories and Crown Dependencies must be added there first, each with the ISO code the region-of-origin prefix will use, and the four EFTA entries removed. Whether to follow DR1's naming of Czech Republic, Republic of Ireland and Netherlands is part of the same list decision. Because both pages read one function, the frontend side is a single change once the data exists.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding any territory or Crown Dependency offered on the frontend's origin or destination-country select — neither captured DOM contains Azores, Guernsey, Jersey or Isle of Man, and neither string appears in the frontend's country fixtures.
finding.verification: Counted the option elements in all four captured DOMs and listed them out: fe-origin and fe-destination-country each carry 33 options (placeholder, divider, 31 countries) ending at Switzerland; the transit reveal's transitDestinationCountry select carries 42 (placeholder plus 41). Enumerated DR1's 41 and they are exactly 27 member states, the 11 named territories and the 3 named Crown Dependencies, so every name quoted in the prototype slot is verbatim. Confirmed the three naming differences in the rendered markup — "Czechia" against "Czech Republic", "Ireland" against "Republic of Ireland", "Netherlands (the)" against "Netherlands". Opened both origin screenshots. Re-resolved all four citations: origin/controller.js:57-61 and destination-country/controller.js:24-28 are both the countryItems spread of countries.originCountries(), and services/countries/index.js:11 is the fetchCountries(['GBNAG_SPS_EX']) call. Ran the falsifier: grep for Azores, Guernsey, Jersey, Isle of Man and the other nine territories across src/server/app returns nothing, and the countries-origin.json fixture holds 31 entries with none of them. Band checked against rubric 6 and the source rather than accepted — services/countries/client.js fetches /countries from the reference-data service, so the frontend cannot edit the list. CORRECT.
finding.correction: No claim falsified. Two refinements, neither changing the slots. (1) The dependency is understated rather than wrong: reference-data does not own these names either — Country.java builds each entry from an MdmCountry (getEffectiveAlpha2 / getEffectiveAlias), so reference-data proxies DEFRA MDM and the territories have to reach MDM before reference-data can serve them. `needs-backend` is right and if anything the chain is one hop longer than the difference slot says. (2) Crop risk under rubric 8: on dr1-origin-of-the-import the name `countryOfOrigin` belongs to a hidden input (the search control writes into it), so a crop keyed on that name resolves to a zero-size box on the DR1 side. The frontend side crops fine.

relatedTo.why: DR1 derives the region-of-origin prefix from the selected country, so the codes behind these entries are what that prefix reads
